scope: Rebuild equipment mounting and rail around the selected common bought carbon adapter, retaining the separate servo/input and propulsion/output assemblies.
intentional_changes: Four identical 30 × 30 × 1 mm bought carbon adapters carry the battery, FC, navigation module and F-Mini. Bespoke printed equipment decks, rail shoes and the FC saddle are removed. Undimensioned carbon cutouts are not reconstructed.

One 340 mm twin-track PA12 rail clamps the rotated 16 mm Y-axis hole pair using ordinary M2 screws and nuts. Seven 42 mm flat bays at 48 mm pitch provide ±6 mm supported trim about each bay centre. Larger moves require lifting and reinstalling the plate. Unbolted nuts must be supported from below before the rail is taped to the balloon.

The propulsion frame uses its own 3 mm thick direct foot on the tracks. Raising the complete propulsion module by 4.8 mm preserves the 51 protected local drive, gear, bearing and horn solids and their local transforms. The paired servo/input module remains separately replaceable.

Default station X coordinates are battery +96, propulsion +3, FC −51 and accessory −123 mm; navigation lies at −147 and F-Mini at −101 mm. The FC retains a 9 mm peripheral wiring band and 8 mm underbody allowance. F-Mini is rotated 90°. Nominal 3 mm insulating pads clear modeled clamp heads; real pad compression and supported contact remain unverified.

A removable one-piece optical portal uses the two 25.5 mm X-axis carbon holes independently of the rail clamps. The battery host adds two M2×6 screw/nut pairs. The FC host reuses two existing studs and raises their intermediate nuts above the feet. The portal top is 51.3 mm above the rail datum; both optical profiles and hosts are checked.

An optional one-piece power portal adds two upper bought carbon boards and uses the same lower attachment interface. Lower boards remain installed and are included in interference checks. Retaining all lower boards with this option requires six carbon boards in total.

Legacy side-clamp controls and continuous end-slide claims are removed. Service checks include device removal before top-clamp access, long-leg hex-key access, then ordered battery/portal and servo/input removal before propulsion service. Fine trim is limited by the actual flat bay geometry.

Preview now re-reads live CAD registry objects after optical-host transfer, which recreates battery foot fasteners. Assembly validation also defensively refreshes its object list and verifies exact registry membership. These lifecycle fixes do not alter geometry.

STL surface comparison accounts for a mathematically bounded float32 rounding cell only for meshes with exactly identical serialized vertex sets. Changed vertex sets retain the original tolerance; bidirectional coverage and topology checks remain required. Retriangulation is distinguished from missing or displaced surface.

Recreated optical-foot fasteners retain their original position in the optical hardware block after host transfers, so preview restores the exact hardware registry sequence as well as the same physical parts. The strict pinned-baseline comparison remains unchanged.
tradeoffs: Installed printed parts decrease from 12 to 10; modeled bought hardware items increase from 69 to 84. This standardizes the mounts and reduces modeled mass, but does not reduce the total installed item count.

The rail itself is heavier. Removing printed carriers reduces printed mass by 10.969 g; added hardware contributes 5.255 g, giving a net modeled reduction of 5.714 g. Real insulation, adhesive, wiring, FC upper mounting hardware and unmeasured components are excluded.
Discrete flat bays replace full-length sliding. Actual balloon curvature, tape engagement and rail flexure fatigue require physical qualification.

The carbon adapters carry light equipment and portal loads. Actual cutouts, contact areas and laminate bending must be checked before manufacturing approval; conservative CAD envelopes do not establish supported material.
physical_limits: CAD prototype only; no manufacturing or flight release. PA12 grade, process, finish and supplier acceptance of one-piece 340 mm printing remain unresolved.
Actual carbon dimensions, cutouts, supported contact, insulation, battery overhang and strap retention are unverified.
The actual FC damping and upper hardware stack, shaft/bearing fits, printed clamp creep, loaded horn/gear travel and moving wire loops remain unqualified.
Optional power sharing, connected harnesses, tether retention and RF/antenna performance remain unqualified.

final_verification.status: CAD prototype verification passed; physical qualification remains unresolved

superseded_attempts.reason: Preview accessed deleted opticalfoot handles afterhosttransfer; stoppedbeforevalidate.

Build and preview passed. ContinuousRail STL comparison failed at a fixed 0.00001 mm slab despite identical serialized vertices. Only triangulation differed; numerical rounding exceeded that slab at the long rail coordinates. Other geometry, equipment and optional-power checks passed.

Build, preview and full validation passed. Strict baseline comparison rejected reordered HardwareParts after optical-host round-trip. All 136 shape comparisons, placements, metadata and controls passed. Actual registry order restoration is fixed instead of relaxing baseline comparison.
